<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par65"/>Exceptions, in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=אסלוח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=7}}, {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֶסְלַח}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}); in the {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=טְבֹחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=16}}. On such cases as {{GHGheb|text=אֶפְשֳׂעָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=4}}, cf. {{GHGpar|10|h}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|65|c}}
(''c'') Where {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} would be the regular vowel of the final syllable, both forms (with ''ē<sup>a</sup>'' and ''ă'') are sometimes in use; the choice of one or the other is decided by the special circumstances of the tone, i.e.:—

{{GHGmargin-letter|65|d}}
Rem. 1. In the {{GHGterm|absolute state}} of the {{GHGterm|participle Qal}}, {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}, the forms {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁלֵחַ}} (with suff. {{GHGheb|text=שֹֽׁלְחִי}}, but {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁלֵֽחֲךָ}}), {{GHGheb|text=מְשַׁלֵּחַ}} (with suff. {{GHGheb|text=מְשַׁלּֽחֲךָ}}), and {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁתַּגֵּעַ}} are used exclusively; except in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ע}} where we find, in close connexion, also {{GHGheb|text=נֹטַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=94|verse=9}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֹגַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=35}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֹקַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=רוֹקַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=136|verse=6}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁסָע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=11|verse=7}}, all with the tone on the last syllable.—The part. Puʿal is {{GHGheb|text=מְרֻבַּע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=45|verse=2}} according to the best authorities (Kittel {{GHGheb|text=מְרֻבָּע}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|65|e}}
2. Similarly, in the ''imperf.'' and ''inf. Niphʿal'', and in the ''perf. inf.'' and ''imperf. Piʿēl'' the (probably more original) form with ''ă'' commonly occurs in the body of the sentence, and the fuller form with ''ē<sup>a</sup>'' in {{GHGterm|pause}} (and even with the lesser distinctives, e.g. with ''D<sup>e</sup>hi'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=86|verse=4}} in the {{GHGterm|imperative Piʿēl}}; with {{GHGterm|Ṭiphḥa}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=32}} in the {{GHGterm|infinitive Piʿēl}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=31}} {{GHGterm|imperfect Hithpaʿēl}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=16|verse=6}} {{GHGterm|imperfect Niphʿal}}), cf. e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִגָּרַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=27|verse=4}}, with {{GHGheb|text=יִגָּרֵעַֽ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=36|verse=3|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּשָּׁבַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=34}}, even with retraction of the tone in the ''inf. abs. Niphʿal'' {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּׁבַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=30|verse=3}} (elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּׁבֵעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=7|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=12|verse=16|hidebook=1}} twice, in each case without the pause); {{GHGheb|text=תְּבַקַּע־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=9}}, with {{GHGheb|text=תְּבַקֵּֽעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=בַּלַּע|translate=to devour}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=1|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=4|verse=20}} with {{GHGheb|text=בַּלֵּ֑עַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=8}}; for {{GHGterm|infinitive Hithpaʿēl}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=20}}. The ''infinitive absolute Piʿē̇l'' has the from {{GHGheb|text=שַׁלֵּחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=22|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=22}}; the {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}}, on the other hand, when without the pause is always as {{GHGheb|text=שַׁלַּח}} except {{GHGheb|text=לְשַׁלֵּחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=4}}.— {{GHGheb|text=יְזַבֵּחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=1|verse=16}} has ''ē'', though not in {{GHGterm|pause}}, and even {{GHGheb|text=וַיְזַבֵּחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=16|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=4}}; but ''a'' in {{GHGterm|pause}} in the {{GHGterm|imperative Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵֽאָנַ֑ח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=11}}; ''jussive Piʿēl'' {{GHGheb|text=תְּאַחַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=40|verse=18}}; cf. {{GHGpar|52|n}}. An example of ''ă'' in the {{GHGterm|imperative Piʿēl}} under the influence of a final {{GHGheb|text=ר}} is {{GHGheb|text=כַּתַּר־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=36|verse=2}}, in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=וָתֵּֽעָצַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=13}}, &c.—In {{GHGheb|text=יַפְרִחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=9}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=92|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=11}}), Barth (see above, {{GHGpar|63|n}}) finds an ''i-imperfect'' of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, since the intransitive meaning is only found in {{GHGterm|Qal}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|65|f}}
3. In the 2nd ''sing. masc.'' of the {{GHGterm|imperative}}, and in the forms of the {{GHGterm|jussive}} and {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} which end in gutturals, ''a'' alone occurs, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַצְלַח|translate=prosper thou}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַבְטַח|translate=let him make to trust}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּצְמַח|translate=and he made to grow}} (so in ''Hithpalpel'' {{GHGheb|text=יִחְמַהְמַהּ}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=3}}); even in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּצְלַ֑ח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=29|verse=23}}, and, with the best authorities, {{GHGheb|text=וְיוֹכָֽח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=12|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְישַֽׁעֲכֶ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=35|verse=4}} is perhaps to be emended into {{GHGheb|text=וְישִֽׁעֲ׳}} (={{GHGheb|text=וְיוֹשִׁיע׳}}).—In the ''infinitive absolute Ṣere'' remains, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַגְבֵּהַּ|translate=to make high}}; as {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} {{GHGheb|text=חוֹכַח}} also occurs in close connexion ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=26}}); on {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשֵׁעַ}} as {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=26.33}}), cf. {{GHGpar|53|k}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|65|g}}
'''2.''' When the guttural with {{GHGterm|quiescent Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} stands at the end of a syllable, the ordinary strong form remains when not connected with suffixes, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלַ֫חְתָּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלַ֫חְתִּי}}. But in the 2nd ''sing. fem. perfect'' a ''helping-Pathaḥ'' takes the place of the {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכַ֫חַתְּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=25}} ({{GHGpar|28|e}}); also in, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=3}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָקַ֫חַתְּ}} is to be read, not {{GHGheb|text=לָקַחְתְּ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|65|h}}
Rem. The soft combination with {{GHGterm|compound Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} occurs only in the 1st ''plur. perfect'' with suffixes, since in these forms the tone is thrown one place farther forward, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יְדַֽעֲנ֫וּךָ|translate=we know thee}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=8|verse=2}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=132|verse=6|hidebook=1}}). Before the ''suffixes'' {{GHGheb|text=ךָ}} and {{GHGheb|text=בֶם}}, the guttural must have {{GHGheb|text=־ֲ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֶשְׁלָֽחֲךָ|translate=I will send thee}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֲשַׁלֵּֽחֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=27}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַשְׁמִֽיעֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=18|verse=2}}.

On the weak verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}}, see especially § 74.<section end="par65"/><noinclude>
